practice.q: The server is registered as mcpServers: { nova } and the tool is called kb_search. Finish the allow rule.
practice.hint: mcp, two underscores, the server key, two underscores, the tool name.
practice.why: Allow rules match the full name the model calls: mcp__<server>__<tool>.

practice.q: What does the third argument of tool() expect?

options.why: tool() takes a zod shape, the plain object of fields, not a z.object() schema.
A plain object of zod fields. The SDK builds the schema and checks every call against it.

options.text: A JSON Schema object such as { type: "object", properties: { ... } }
options.why: In TypeScript, tool() takes zod. The SDK turns it into JSON Schema for the model.

practice.q: Put one call to kb_search in order, from the model's decision to the answer.
items: The model reads kb_search's description and decides to call it
The model sends arguments that should match the schema
The SDK checks the arguments against the zod shape
Your handler runs and returns a text block
The text goes back to the model as the tool result
practice.why: Validation happens before your handler, so a wrong argument never reaches your code; the result always goes back to the model, not to you.

practice.q: kb_search found nothing. Which return value helps the model most?

options.why: An empty success looks like a real answer with no content. The model may guess.
The model gets the raw message, which works, but you lose the chance to say what to try next.

options.text: { content: [{ type: "text", text: "No page matches; try a shorter question" }], isError: true }
options.why: A failed result with a useful next step: the model knows it failed and how to retry.

practice.q: Mark kb_search as a tool with no side effects, so it can run in parallel with other read-only tools.
practice.hint: An MCP annotation whose name says the tool only reads.
practice.why: readOnlyHint lets the SDK run the tool alongside other read-only calls. It is a hint, not a wall: keep it true to what the handler does.
